Subject: Renewal: term alignment + staged capacity uplift (MSA & order form redlines)

Hi Emma — great kickoff yesterday. Per our call, Lighthouse is targeting a renewal that: (1) extends term to 24 months, (2) adds a phased capacity uplift (Q1 +30%, Q3 +40%), and (3) introduces a tapered billing schedule for the first two quarters to smooth your cashflow.

Attached are two working files: LH_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf and a draft MSA redline (MSA_2026_redline_notes.docx). Key items we wanted to surface for legal: 
- Term: proposed 24 months (with a mutual early-exit clause tied to specific SLA misses).
- Billing/proration: pilot months to be billed at 50% for the incremental capacity; full uplift billing starts after the second quarter.
- SLA credits: cap to be negotiated — propose standard Redwood SLA credit table but add an exception for scheduled maintenance windows.
- Data residency: keep EU data routing for EU tenants (no change), US tenants unaffected.

Can you confirm if your procurement/legal can accept staged proration language (see redline p.3) or whether you need firm monthly billing? Also looping Dev for the technical coverage schedule.

Next steps: if legal has high-level signoff on term and proration approach, we'll consolidate redlines into a single order form and share the DocuSign link for signature routing.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the docs and recap. Our procurement/legal reviewed and have two immediate asks: 
1) They won't accept a unilateral early-exit tied to SLA misses without a remediation/cure period (they're asking 60 days).
2) For proration, FP&A prefers an invoice schedule that doesn't vary month-to-month within a quarter — they asked if the staged uplift could be represented as a fixed monthly increment for each quarter (i.e., Q1: +10%/mo to reach +30% by month three) rather than a single quarter-end charge.

Also legal has one redline on indemnity language in the MSA (they want narrower IP carveouts). Attaching our terse summary as PDF; legal will send the markups formally.

Can you loop in your legal to confirm the cure period and indemnity stance?

Marissa / Dev — forwarding Emma's notes. Quick legal read: 
- Early-exit for SLA misses: we can accept a 60-day cure period, but we should preserve Redwood's right to fix/mitigate and limit termination to repeated breaches (2 within a 12-month period). Proposed redline included in MSA_2026_redline_notes.docx (see section 6.2).
- Indemnity: we will push back on narrowing the IP carveouts too far; propose middle ground language that retains our standard IP defense but limits consequential damages to the extent permitted by law.
- Billing/proration: finance ops can accommodate their preferred fixed-monthly-increment approach — operationally it's fine — but we need explicit language in the order form that maps the uplift schedule to invoicing buckets (see Capacity_Uplift_Schedule.xlsx).

Two asks for Marissa: please confirm whether Lighthouse expects the uplift to be available from a dedicated pool (Dedicated capacity) or on-hosted shared hosts — that affects pricing/scoping. Also share the procurement contact for signature routing.

Olga

Emma — quick follow-up on technical/ops questions: 
- We can provision the phased uplift on your existing Dedicated pool with capacity reservations. That will preserve latency SLAs. Pricing in the order form assumes dedicated reservation for the uplift.
- If you want to keep uplift on hosted shared capacity, we can, but we'd need to add burst-headroom protections and the price per uplift unit is ~12% higher.
- Expected lead time for capacity resizing: 3-5 business days after signature for a dedicated pool; immediate for shared but with risk of transient throttling.

I'll flag this in the order form and add a short paragraph under "Provisioning & Lead Time". If you prefer dedicated, say so and we'll lock pricing and add a provisioning SOW line.
